![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/c21d4794aeedcc70fe037a936724d2708a484d43c457b2d120927f86f1fa6ffc.png)

The region enclosed by the curve $y={x}^{2}-2x-2$ and the horizontal line $y=-2$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=-2.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curve and the line by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x-2 & =-2 \\ {x}^{2}-2x & =0 \\ x(x-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=2$ along the $x$-axis. 

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/e785138362c91f9034d90ee9d923fc818cd299b3ee5d6d25eb1bf40cabc2f2b0.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y={x}^{2}-2x-2,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=-2.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}{[\,(-2)-({x}^{2}-2x-2)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(-{x}^{2}+2x)^{2}\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}-{x}^{4}+\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}\text{ })|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\pi ([\frac{1}{5}(2)^{5}-(2)^{4}+\frac{4}{3}(2)^{3}\text{ }]-[0]) \\  & =\pi (\frac{32}{5}-16+\frac{32}{3}) \\  & =\frac{16\pi }{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
